paragraphs.title: The Law of the Guilt Offering

easy.question: What offering is described at the beginning of the passage?
answers: A guilt offering
A thanksgiving offering
A Passover offering
easy.explanation: The passage begins, “This is the law of the trespass offering.”

easy.question: Where was the guilt offering to be slaughtered?
answers: Outside the camp
Where the burnt offering was slaughtered
At the priest’s house
easy.explanation: It was slaughtered “in the place where they kill the burnt offering.”

easy.question: Who was permitted to eat the guilt offering?
answers: Anyone from Israel
Only the person who brought it
Every male among the priests
easy.explanation: Verse 6 says, “Every male among the priests shall eat thereof.”

medium.question: What was done with the blood of the guilt offering after it was slaughtered?
answers: It was sprinkled around the altar
It was poured outside the camp
It was given to the person who brought the offering
medium.explanation: The blood was sprinkled around the altar, as stated in verse 2.

medium.question: What order of actions is described for the guilt offering?
answers: Eating the meat, slaughtering it, and sprinkling the blood
Slaughtering it, sprinkling the blood, and burning the prescribed parts
Burning the parts, eating the meat, and then slaughtering it
medium.explanation: First it was slaughtered, then its blood was sprinkled, and finally its parts were burned on the altar.

medium.question: According to the verse, what was done with the part described as “the caul that is above the liver”?
answers: It was left on the animal’s skin
It was given to the person bringing the offering
It was removed with the kidneys and burned on the altar
medium.explanation: The verse lists it with the kidneys among the parts removed and burned as an offering.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the guilt offering was like the burnt offering in the location of slaughter, but not necessarily in its rules of consumption?
answers: It was slaughtered where the burnt offering was slaughtered, but the priests ate it
All Israelites ate it
It had no connection with the altar
challenge.explanation: The verse compares the place of slaughter, but later says that every male priest may eat it.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “As the sin offering is, so is the guilt offering: there is one law for them”?
answers: The sin offering and guilt offering were exactly the same
They shared a rule, including that the officiating priest received the offering
Only the high priest could eat both offerings
challenge.explanation: The statement establishes a shared law, and the priest who made atonement received the offering.

challenge.question: Which combination correctly describes how the guilt offering was divided between the altar and the priests?
answers: The entire offering was eaten, and nothing was burned
The blood was eaten, and the meat was sprinkled around the altar
The prescribed fat and inner parts were burned, while the rest was eaten by male priests in a holy place
challenge.explanation: The fat and prescribed inner parts were burned on the altar; the remaining guilt offering was eaten by the priests.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the guilt offering was like the burnt offering in the location of slaughter, but not necessarily in its rules of consumption?
answers: It was slaughtered where the burnt offering was slaughtered, but the priests ate it
All Israelites ate it
It had no connection with the altar
questions.explanation: The verse compares the place of slaughter, but later says that every male priest may eat it.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “As the sin offering is, so is the guilt offering: there is one law for them”?
answers: The sin offering and guilt offering were exactly the same
They shared a rule, including that the officiating priest received the offering
Only the high priest could eat both offerings
questions.explanation: The statement establishes a shared law, and the priest who made atonement received the offering.

questions.question: Which combination correctly describes how the guilt offering was divided between the altar and the priests?
answers: The entire offering was eaten, and nothing was burned
The blood was eaten, and the meat was sprinkled around the altar
The prescribed fat and inner parts were burned, while the rest was eaten by male priests in a holy place
questions.explanation: The fat and prescribed inner parts were burned on the altar; the remaining guilt offering was eaten by the priests.

paragraphs.title: The Priests’ Portions of the Offerings

easy.question: To whom did the skin of the burnt offering belong?
answers: To the priest who offered it
To all the sons of Aaron
To the person who brought the offering
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The priest shall have to himself the skin of the burnt offering.”

easy.question: Who received a grain offering baked in an oven or prepared in a frying pan?
answers: All the sons of Aaron
The priest who offered it
The person who brought it
easy.explanation: The verse says that these offerings belonged to the priest who offered them.

easy.question: Who received a grain offering mixed with oil or a dry offering?
answers: Only the priest who offered it
The person who brought the offering
All the sons of Aaron
easy.explanation: The verse assigns these offerings to all the sons of Aaron, one as much as another.

medium.question: What did offerings baked in an oven, prepared in a frying pan, and prepared in a pan have in common?
answers: The priest who offered them received them
They were divided among all the sons of Aaron
They were given to the person who brought them
medium.explanation: All three forms of preparation are said to belong to the priest who offered the offering.

medium.question: In the phrase “mingled with oil, and dry,” what does “dry” mean?
answers: Burned in a fire
Not mixed with oil
Prepared in an oven
medium.explanation: “Dry” contrasts with “mingled with oil,” indicating an offering without oil mixed into it.

medium.question: What was the difference between receiving the skin of the burnt offering and receiving the grain offerings?
answers: The skin went to the person bringing the offering, while the grain offerings went to the priests
The skin was divided among everyone, while the grain offerings went to one priest
The skin and the offering prepared by the priest went to that priest, but an oil-mixed or dry offering went to all the sons of Aaron
medium.explanation: The skin and certain offerings went to the officiating priest, while the oil-mixed or dry offering went to all Aaron’s sons.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “The priest who offers it shall have it”?
answers: The right was connected to the priest who performed the offering
All priests always received equal portions
Only the person bringing the offering could receive it
challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes the particular priest who offered the sacrifice or grain offering.

challenge.question: What does “one as much as another” teach about the oil-mixed and dry offerings?
answers: Only one brother received them
Aaron’s sons received them equally
They could be eaten only by biological brothers
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates an equal distribution among the sons of Aaron.

challenge.question: One priest offered a burnt offering, and another offered a grain offering baked in an oven. What did each receive?
answers: Both received all the grain offerings
The first received the grain offering, and the second received the burnt offering’s skin
The first received the burnt offering’s skin, and the second received the grain offering he baked
challenge.explanation: The skin belonged to the priest who offered the burnt offering, and the baked offering belonged to the priest who offered it.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “The priest who offers it shall have it”?
answers: The right was connected to the priest who performed the offering
All priests always received equal portions
Only the person bringing the offering could receive it
questions.explanation: The wording emphasizes the particular priest who offered the sacrifice or grain offering.

questions.question: What does “one as much as another” teach about the oil-mixed and dry offerings?
answers: Only one brother received them
Aaron’s sons received them equally
They could be eaten only by biological brothers
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates an equal distribution among the sons of Aaron.

questions.question: One priest offered a burnt offering, and another offered a grain offering baked in an oven. What did each receive?
answers: Both received all the grain offerings
The first received the grain offering, and the second received the burnt offering’s skin
The first received the burnt offering’s skin, and the second received the grain offering he baked
questions.explanation: The skin belonged to the priest who offered the burnt offering, and the baked offering belonged to the priest who offered it.

paragraphs.title: The Thanksgiving Offering and Its Consumption

easy.question: What type of sacrifice is described at the beginning of the passage?
answers: A peace offering
A sin offering
A guilt offering
easy.explanation: Verse 11 says, “This is the law of the sacrifice of peace offerings.”

easy.question: What was offered with a thanksgiving sacrifice?
answers: Meat alone
Various kinds of bread
Oil alone
easy.explanation: The passage describes unleavened cakes, wafers, fine-flour cakes, and leavened bread.

easy.question: When was the meat of the thanksgiving offering to be eaten?
answers: On the day it was offered
The following morning
After three days
easy.explanation: Verse 15 says that its flesh was to be eaten the same day and not left until morning.

medium.question: What was distinctive about the thanksgiving offering compared with the general description of a peace offering?
answers: It contained no meat
It was accompanied by several kinds of bread
It was eaten only after a week
medium.explanation: The thanksgiving offering included several kinds of unleavened bread as well as leavened bread.

medium.question: In the phrase “one out of the whole oblation for an heave offering,” what does “heave offering” mean?
answers: A song of thanksgiving
A sacred utensil
A portion lifted up and dedicated
medium.explanation: The verse describes one portion set apart and dedicated to the Lord.

medium.question: Who received the portion set apart from the offering?
answers: The priest who sprinkled the blood of the peace offerings
Every Israelite
Only the person who brought the offering
medium.explanation: Verse 14 says it belonged to the priest who sprinkled the blood of the peace offerings.

challenge.question: What might be surprising about the bread offered with the thanksgiving sacrifice?
answers: All the bread had to be leavened
All the bread had to be unleavened
It included both unleavened cakes and leavened bread
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions unleavened breads and also says that leavened bread was offered.

challenge.question: What follows from the command not to leave any of the thanksgiving offering’s flesh until morning?
answers: It had to be finished on the day it was offered
It could be eaten only in the morning
None of it could be eaten
challenge.explanation: The command to eat it on the day of offering, together with the prohibition against leaving it overnight, requires same-day consumption.

challenge.question: According to the order of the verses, what happened after the offering and breads were presented?
answers: The meat was left until morning
A portion of the offering was set apart for the priest
The priest’s service ended
challenge.explanation: The passage next says that one portion was set apart for the priest who sprinkled the blood, then describes when the meat was eaten.

questions.question: What might be surprising about the bread offered with the thanksgiving sacrifice?
answers: All the bread had to be leavened
All the bread had to be unleavened
It included both unleavened cakes and leavened bread
questions.explanation: The passage mentions unleavened breads and also says that leavened bread was offered.

questions.question: What follows from the command not to leave any of the thanksgiving offering’s flesh until morning?
answers: It had to be finished on the day it was offered
It could be eaten only in the morning
None of it could be eaten
questions.explanation: The command to eat it on the day of offering, together with the prohibition against leaving it overnight, requires same-day consumption.

questions.question: According to the order of the verses, what happened after the offering and breads were presented?
answers: The meat was left until morning
A portion of the offering was set apart for the priest
The priest’s service ended
questions.explanation: The passage next says that one portion was set apart for the priest who sprinkled the blood, then describes when the meat was eaten.

paragraphs.title: Vows, Freewill Offerings, and the Time of Eating

easy.question: On which days could the meat of a vow or freewill offering be eaten?
answers: On the day it was offered and the following day
Only on the third day
Throughout the week
easy.explanation: The passage permits eating it on the day of the offering and on the next day.

easy.question: What was to be done with meat remaining on the third day?
answers: It was given to the poor
It was burned with fire
It was eaten immediately
easy.explanation: The passage says that the remaining meat was to be burned on the third day.

easy.question: What was the sacrifice called if its meat was eaten on the third day?
answers: Clean
Accepted
An abomination
easy.explanation: The passage says that eating it on the third day made it unacceptable and defiled.

medium.question: Why was the meat remaining on the third day to be burned?
answers: Because the offering could be eaten only through the second day
Because the sacrifice became more valuable
Because the third day was the day it was offered
medium.explanation: It could be eaten on the offering day and the next day; anything remaining on the third day was not to be eaten.

medium.question: In the phrase “the remainder of it shall be eaten,” what does “remainder” mean?
answers: The meat eaten first
The meat that remained
The meat that was burned
medium.explanation: “Remainder” means what was left; in context, it was eaten on the second day.

medium.question: What was the result of eating the sacrifice’s meat on the third day?
answers: The sacrifice became more acceptable
It could be eaten without restriction
The sacrifice was not accepted, and the eater bore guilt
medium.explanation: The passage says the offering would not be accepted and that the person who ate it bore his iniquity.

challenge.question: Which sequence matches the passage?
answers: The sacrifice was offered, eaten on the first and second days, and the remainder burned on the third day
The sacrifice was burned on the first day and eaten on the third
The sacrifice was eaten on the third day and offered afterward
challenge.explanation: The offering came first, eating was permitted for two days, and the remainder was burned on the third.

challenge.question: What does “it shall not be accepted” teach about a sacrifice eaten on the third day?
answers: It would be accepted even more readily
It would not be regarded as acceptable before the Lord
It had to be eaten only by priests
challenge.explanation: The phrase means that the sacrifice would no longer be accepted as proper.

challenge.question: What distinction does the passage make regarding someone who ate on the third day?
answers: Only the one offering it was punished
The sacrifice was not accepted for the one offering it, and the eater bore guilt
The eater was considered righteous because the meat had been kept for a long time
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions both the offering’s rejection and the eater’s guilt.

questions.question: Which sequence matches the passage?
answers: The sacrifice was offered, eaten on the first and second days, and the remainder burned on the third day
The sacrifice was burned on the first day and eaten on the third
The sacrifice was eaten on the third day and offered afterward
questions.explanation: The offering came first, eating was permitted for two days, and the remainder was burned on the third.

questions.question: What does “it shall not be accepted” teach about a sacrifice eaten on the third day?
answers: It would be accepted even more readily
It would not be regarded as acceptable before the Lord
It had to be eaten only by priests
questions.explanation: The phrase means that the sacrifice would no longer be accepted as proper.

questions.question: What distinction does the passage make regarding someone who ate on the third day?
answers: Only the one offering it was punished
The sacrifice was not accepted for the one offering it, and the eater bore guilt
The eater was considered righteous because the meat had been kept for a long time
questions.explanation: The passage mentions both the offering’s rejection and the eater’s guilt.

paragraphs.title: Uncleanness and Eating the Peace Offering

easy.question: What was to be done with meat that touched anything unclean?
answers: It was eaten immediately
It was burned with fire
It was saved for the next day
easy.explanation: Meat that touched anything unclean was not to be eaten but burned with fire.

easy.question: Who was permitted to eat the meat?
answers: Anyone
Only the priests
Anyone who was clean
easy.explanation: The passage says, “All that be clean shall eat thereof.”

easy.question: What was the punishment for an unclean person who ate the peace offering’s meat?
answers: He was cut off from his people
He only had to bathe
He had to bring another offering
easy.explanation: The passage says that such a person would be cut off from his people.

medium.question: What sequence is described in verse 19?
answers: The meat touches something unclean, so it is not eaten and is burned
A clean person eats it, and afterward the meat is burned
The meat is burned, and then an unclean person eats it
medium.explanation: The meat first becomes unclean, and consequently it may not be eaten and must be burned.

medium.question: In the phrase “shall be cut off from his people,” what does “cut off” mean?
answers: To become unclean briefly
To be punished by separation from the people
To be required to bring a grain offering
medium.explanation: The phrase describes removal or separation from the community.

medium.question: What kinds of uncleanness are mentioned in verse 21?
answers: Only human uncleanness
Only animal uncleanness
Human uncleanness, an unclean animal, and an unclean abominable thing
medium.explanation: The verse lists human uncleanness, an unclean beast, and an unclean abominable thing.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between unclean meat and an unclean person?
answers: In both cases eating is permitted after bathing
The meat is burned, while the person who eats while unclean is cut off from the people
The meat is cut off from the people, while the person is burned
challenge.explanation: Unclean meat was burned; an unclean person who ate the peace offering faced being cut off.

challenge.question: What shared condition in verses 20–21 leads to being cut off?
answers: An unclean person eats the meat of the peace offering
A clean person touches the meat
The peace offering is kept until morning
challenge.explanation: Both verses concern someone who is unclean yet eats meat belonging to the peace offering.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the contrast between “all that be clean shall eat thereof” and “shall not be eaten”?
answers: All meat is forbidden
Permission to eat depends on both the person’s cleanness and the meat’s condition
Only the person who prepared the offering could eat it
challenge.explanation: The passage permits eating by clean people but forbids eating when the meat or eater is unclean.

questions.question: What is the main difference between unclean meat and an unclean person?
answers: In both cases eating is permitted after bathing
The meat is burned, while the person who eats while unclean is cut off from the people
The meat is cut off from the people, while the person is burned
questions.explanation: Unclean meat was burned; an unclean person who ate the peace offering faced being cut off.

questions.question: What shared condition in verses 20–21 leads to being cut off?
answers: An unclean person eats the meat of the peace offering
A clean person touches the meat
The peace offering is kept until morning
questions.explanation: Both verses concern someone who is unclean yet eats meat belonging to the peace offering.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the contrast between “all that be clean shall eat thereof” and “shall not be eaten”?
answers: All meat is forbidden
Permission to eat depends on both the person’s cleanness and the meat’s condition
Only the person who prepared the offering could eat it
questions.explanation: The passage permits eating by clean people but forbids eating when the meat or eater is unclean.

paragraphs.title: The Prohibition of Fat and Blood

easy.question: What was forbidden to eat from an ox, sheep, or goat?
answers: The fat
The meat
The bones
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Ye shall eat no manner of fat, of ox, or of sheep, or of goat.”

easy.question: What was forbidden to eat wherever the Israelites lived?
answers: Salt
Blood
Bread
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Ye shall eat no manner of blood…in any of your dwellings.”

easy.question: What was the penalty for eating forbidden fat or blood?
answers: A sacrifice had to be brought
The person could not leave the camp
The person was cut off from the people
easy.explanation: The passage says that the person who ate it would be cut off from the people.

medium.question: What could be done with the fat of an animal that died naturally or was torn?
answers: It could be used for any other purpose
It could be eaten secretly
It could be offered only on the altar
medium.explanation: The passage permits it to be used for other purposes but forbids eating it.

medium.question: Why was eating fat treated as especially serious in verse 25?
answers: Because it was found only in the wilderness
Because it came from an animal used for an offering made by fire to the Lord
Because fat was difficult to chew
medium.explanation: The verse connects the prohibition with animals from which offerings were made to the Lord.

medium.question: In the phrase “the fat of the beast that dieth of itself, and the fat of that which is torn,” what animals are being described?
answers: Animals born defective
Animals properly offered
Animals that died or were not slaughtered properly
medium.explanation: The context refers to animals that died naturally or were killed by other animals rather than slaughtered properly.

challenge.question: What is the correct distinction between the fat of an animal that died or was torn and blood?
answers: Both may be eaten in certain places
Such fat may be used for other purposes, but blood may not be eaten anywhere
Blood may be used for other purposes, but fat may never be used
challenge.explanation: The passage allows other uses for such fat but prohibits eating blood in any dwelling.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “in any of your dwellings”?
answers: The prohibition on eating blood applied wherever Israelites lived
The prohibition applied only inside the tabernacle
The prohibition applied only during sacrifices
challenge.explanation: The wording extends the prohibition to every place where the Israelites lived.

challenge.question: What conclusion follows from the repeated reference to “the soul” in verses 25 and 27?
answers: Only priests were punished for forbidden eating
The penalty applied only to someone eating sacrificial fat
Anyone who ate blood or forbidden fat could be cut off from the people
challenge.explanation: The verses speak broadly of anyone who eats these forbidden substances.

questions.question: What is the correct distinction between the fat of an animal that died or was torn and blood?
answers: Both may be eaten in certain places
Such fat may be used for other purposes, but blood may not be eaten anywhere
Blood may be used for other purposes, but fat may never be used
questions.explanation: The passage allows other uses for such fat but prohibits eating blood in any dwelling.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “in any of your dwellings”?
answers: The prohibition on eating blood applied wherever Israelites lived
The prohibition applied only inside the tabernacle
The prohibition applied only during sacrifices
questions.explanation: The wording extends the prohibition to every place where the Israelites lived.

questions.question: What conclusion follows from the repeated reference to “the soul” in verses 25 and 27?
answers: Only priests were punished for forbidden eating
The penalty applied only to someone eating sacrificial fat
Anyone who ate blood or forbidden fat could be cut off from the people
questions.explanation: The verses speak broadly of anyone who eats these forbidden substances.

paragraphs.title: Bringing the Peace Offering and Waving the Breast

easy.question: To whom did the Lord speak at the beginning of this passage?
answers: Moses
The priests
The Israelites
easy.explanation: The passage begins, “And the Lord spake unto Moses.”

easy.question: Who was required to bring the peace offering to the Lord?
answers: The priest alone
The person making the offering
The entire nation together
easy.explanation: The passage says that the person offering the sacrifice shall bring it to the Lord.

easy.question: Which part was designated to be waved before the Lord?
answers: The blood
The head
The breast
easy.explanation: The passage says, “the breast…to be waved for a wave offering before the Lord.”

medium.question: What order of actions is described in the passage?
answers: The offerer brings the offering, and afterward the breast is waved
The breast is waved, and only afterward is the offering brought
Moses waves the breast before the offerer arrives
medium.explanation: The offerer first brings the offering and its parts; then the breast is waved before the Lord.

medium.question: What does “to be waved for a wave offering” mean in context?
answers: To be burned with fire
To be lifted or moved as a presentation
To be eaten immediately
medium.explanation: The breast was presented before the Lord through a lifting or waving motion.

medium.question: What did the offerer bring with his own hands?
answers: The breast alone
The blood alone
The offerings made by fire, including the fat with the breast
medium.explanation: The passage says, “His own hands shall bring the offerings of the Lord made by fire,” including the fat and breast.

challenge.question: In “the breast…to be waved,” what does “it” refer to?
answers: The breast
The fat
The entire sacrifice
challenge.explanation: The pronoun refers back to the breast, the part specifically designated for waving.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “His own hands shall bring”?
answers: Only the priest could touch the offering
The offerer himself participated in bringing the offering’s parts
The offering was brought without human involvement
challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes that the offerer personally brought the offering’s parts.

challenge.question: What distinction between the offering’s parts appears in the passage?
answers: The breast was burned and the fat was eaten
The breast and fat were both waved in the same action
The fat was among the offerings made by fire, while the breast was designated for waving
challenge.explanation: The passage identifies the fat with the offerings burned to the Lord and separately designates the breast for waving.

questions.question: In “the breast…to be waved,” what does “it” refer to?
answers: The breast
The fat
The entire sacrifice
questions.explanation: The pronoun refers back to the breast, the part specifically designated for waving.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “His own hands shall bring”?
answers: Only the priest could touch the offering
The offerer himself participated in bringing the offering’s parts
The offering was brought without human involvement
questions.explanation: The wording emphasizes that the offerer personally brought the offering’s parts.

questions.question: What distinction between the offering’s parts appears in the passage?
answers: The breast was burned and the fat was eaten
The breast and fat were both waved in the same action
The fat was among the offerings made by fire, while the breast was designated for waving
questions.explanation: The passage identifies the fat with the offerings burned to the Lord and separately designates the breast for waving.

paragraphs.title: The Priests’ Portions of the Peace Offering

easy.question: What did the priest burn on the altar?
answers: The fat
The breast
The right shoulder
easy.explanation: The passage says, “The priest shall burn the fat upon the altar.”

easy.question: To whom did the breast of the peace offerings belong?
answers: All the Israelites
Aaron and his sons
Only the person who brought the offering
easy.explanation: The passage says that the breast belonged to Aaron and his sons.

easy.question: Which part was given as a contribution to the priest?
answers: The breast
The fat
The right shoulder
easy.explanation: The passage says, “the right shoulder shall ye give unto the priest.”

medium.question: To whom was the right shoulder assigned as a portion?
answers: To the Aaronite priest who offered the blood and fat
To everyone who ate from the sacrifice
To the offerer alone, even if he was not a priest
medium.explanation: The right shoulder belonged to the priest among Aaron’s sons who offered the blood and fat.

medium.question: What order concerning the offering’s parts is described?
answers: The breast was burned, the fat was given to the priest, and the shoulder to the people
The fat was burned, the breast was given to Aaron and his sons, and the shoulder was given to the priest
All parts were given to Aaron and his sons
medium.explanation: The fat was burned on the altar, the breast went to Aaron and his sons, and the right shoulder went to the priest.

medium.question: What does “give unto the priest” mean in context?
answers: A song of thanksgiving
Eating the sacrifice
A portion set apart as a gift for the priest
medium.explanation: The context shows that a designated portion was separated and given to the priest.

challenge.question: What does the explanation beginning with “For” establish?
answers: The breast and shoulder were taken from Israel’s sacrifices and given to Aaron and his sons as a permanent statute
The priest could offer only the shoulder
The Israelites were not allowed to bring peace offerings
challenge.explanation: The passage explains that the Lord took these portions from Israel’s peace offerings and gave them to the priests permanently.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between the breast and the right shoulder?
answers: The breast was burned, while the shoulder was eaten on the altar
The breast went to Aaron and his sons, while the shoulder was assigned to the officiating priest
The breast belonged to Israel, while the shoulder belonged only to the Levites
challenge.explanation: The breast was given to Aaron and his sons; the right shoulder was a portion for the priest who officiated.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the shoulder being assigned “for his part”?
answers: The entire shoulder was burned on the altar
The shoulder could be given to anyone at will
It was a designated portion intended for a particular priest
challenge.explanation: The wording indicates an allotted portion for the Aaronite priest who offered the sacrifice.

questions.question: What does the explanation beginning with “For” establish?
answers: The breast and shoulder were taken from Israel’s sacrifices and given to Aaron and his sons as a permanent statute
The priest could offer only the shoulder
The Israelites were not allowed to bring peace offerings
questions.explanation: The passage explains that the Lord took these portions from Israel’s peace offerings and gave them to the priests permanently.

questions.question: What is the main difference between the breast and the right shoulder?
answers: The breast was burned, while the shoulder was eaten on the altar
The breast went to Aaron and his sons, while the shoulder was assigned to the officiating priest
The breast belonged to Israel, while the shoulder belonged only to the Levites
questions.explanation: The breast was given to Aaron and his sons; the right shoulder was a portion for the priest who officiated.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the shoulder being assigned “for his part”?
answers: The entire shoulder was burned on the altar
The shoulder could be given to anyone at will
It was a designated portion intended for a particular priest
questions.explanation: The wording indicates an allotted portion for the Aaronite priest who offered the sacrifice.

paragraphs.title: The Priestly Gift for All Generations

easy.question: Whom do these verses concern?
answers: Aaron and his sons
Moses and his sons
The king of Israel and his sons
easy.explanation: The verses concern Aaron and his sons and their priestly service.

easy.question: Who commanded that the gift be given to Aaron and his sons?
answers: Moses
The Lord
The Israelites
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Lord commanded it to be given to them.

easy.question: How long was this arrangement to remain in effect?
answers: One year
Until Aaron’s death
As a statute forever throughout their generations
easy.explanation: The passage calls it a statute forever throughout their generations.

medium.question: What was the connection between Aaron and his sons being anointed and their role?
answers: The anointing was connected with their being appointed to serve as priests to the Lord
The anointing was connected with their going to war
The anointing was connected with their becoming kings
medium.explanation: The passage connects their anointing with being presented to minister to the Lord as priests.

medium.question: What does “the portion of the anointing of Aaron, and of the anointing of his sons” refer to?
answers: A special garment
A financial gift
The portion associated with their consecration to the priesthood
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the priestly portion connected with their anointing and dedication.

medium.question: What happened when Aaron and his sons were presented to serve as priests?
answers: They received their appointed portion and began serving the Lord
They left the people of Israel
They built the tabernacle
medium.explanation: The passage describes their presentation and anointing for priestly service.

challenge.question: From whom was the gift to Aaron and his sons said to come?
answers: From Moses alone
From the children of Israel
From Aaron himself
challenge.explanation: The passage says that the Lord commanded it to be given to them from the children of Israel.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “a statute forever throughout their generations”?
answers: The arrangement was temporary
It was intended only for Aaron
It was intended to continue through future generations
challenge.explanation: The wording indicates that the provision was not limited to one generation.

answers: Portions of sacrifices dedicated to the Lord
Israel’s weapons
The priests’ ordinary food

paragraphs.title: The Law of All the Offerings

easy.question: What does the law in these verses concern?
answers: The various types of offerings
The construction of the tabernacle alone
The journeys through the wilderness
easy.explanation: The passage lists the burnt offering, grain offering, sin offering, guilt offering, consecration offerings, and peace offerings.

easy.question: To whom did the Lord give these commands?
answers: Aaron
Moses
All the kings of Israel
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Lord commanded Moses.

easy.question: Where was this command given?
answers: In Egypt
In Jerusalem
At Mount Sinai and in the wilderness of Sinai
easy.explanation: The final verse mentions Mount Sinai and the wilderness of Sinai.

medium.question: What was the purpose of the command given to Moses concerning the offerings?
answers: To teach the Israelites how to bring their offerings
To forbid the Israelites from bringing offerings
To describe only the Israelites’ journeys
medium.explanation: The command was given so that the Israelites could offer their sacrifices to the Lord.

medium.question: In “to offer their oblations unto the Lord,” what does “offer” mean?
answers: To hide the offerings
To bring them before the Lord as sacred worship
To eat them at home
medium.explanation: In context, offering means bringing the sacrifices to the Lord as part of worship.

medium.question: Which sequence fits the passage?
answers: The Israelites offered in the wilderness, and afterward the Lord commanded Moses
Moses commanded the Lord, and afterward the people reached Sinai
The Lord commanded Moses at Sinai, and the command concerned the Israelites’ offerings in the wilderness
medium.explanation: The passage places the command at Sinai and applies it to Israel’s offerings in the wilderness.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the passage listing several kinds of offerings together?
answers: The law included instructions for different sacrificial services
All the offerings were exactly the same
Only one offering was permitted
challenge.explanation: The list presents a broad system of laws for several different offerings.

challenge.question: Which wording emphasizes that the command was given to Moses but intended for Israel?
answers: The phrase “in the wilderness of Sinai”
The wording “the Lord commanded Moses,” followed by “the children of Israel”
The words “the grain offering”
challenge.explanation: The passage first identifies Moses as the recipient and then identifies Israel as those who were to carry out the command.

challenge.question: Why do the verses connect Mount Sinai with the wilderness of Sinai?
answers: To say that the mountain was in Egypt
To show that sacrifices were offered only in Jerusalem
To connect the place where the command was given with Israel’s setting in the wilderness
challenge.explanation: Mount Sinai identifies the place of revelation, while the wilderness of Sinai identifies the setting in which Israel was to obey the command.
